note: First-cut sovereignty spine, 4000 BCE to present. Negative years are BCE. Ancient entries are deliberately low-confidence; see docs/04-eras.md. NOT yet historian-reviewed.

eras.name: Neolithic & Chalcolithic
eras.summary: No states. Village agriculture, craft specialisation, no evidence of rule.

eras.name: Early Harappan
eras.summary: Regional proto-urban cultures converge on shared material norms.

eras.name: Indus Civilisation
eras.summary: Urban, standardised, long-distance trade — and no evidence of kings or armies.

eras.name: Late Harappan & Vedic
eras.summary: Deurbanisation, eastward shift, oral corpus, emergence of janapadas.

eras.name: Second Urbanisation
eras.summary: Mahajanapadas, punch-marked coinage, Buddhism and Jainism, Magadhan ascent.

eras.name: Mauryan
eras.summary: First subcontinental empire. Edicts, provincial administration, dhamma.

eras.name: Classical
eras.summary: Fragmentation and Indian Ocean trade. Satavahanas, Kushans, Sangam south.

eras.name: Gupta & Post-Gupta
eras.summary: Land-grant economy, temple building, Huna invasions, Harsha.

eras.name: Early Medieval
eras.summary: Regional kingdoms, tripartite struggle, Chola maritime reach, agrarian expansion.

eras.name: Sultanate
eras.summary: Iqta assignment, Vijayanagara and the Deccan sultanates, regional sultanates.

eras.name: Mughal & Early Modern
eras.summary: Mansabdari and zabt revenue, Maratha expansion, European trading companies.

eras.name: Company & Crown
eras.summary: Land revenue settlements, railways, paramountcy, the Drain.

polities.name: Mehrgarh
polities.note: Earliest farming in the region; wheat, barley, cattle.

polities.name: Bhirrana–Ghaggar Neolithic
polities.note: Contested early dates on the Ghaggar-Hakra.

polities.name: South Indian Ashmound Neolithic
polities.note: Cattle pastoralism; ashmounds of the Deccan.

polities.name: Burzahom & Kashmir Neolithic
polities.note: Pit dwellings; links north toward Central Asia.

polities.name: Early Harappan (Ravi / Kot Diji / Sothi-Siswal)
polities.note: Regional cultures converging on shared norms.

polities.name: Indus Civilisation
polities.note: Standardised weights, script, planned cities. No palaces, no royal burials, no army. Modelled as a network, not a state.

polities.name: Sindhi domain (Mohenjo-daro)
polities.note: Regional domain of the Indus network.

polities.name: Punjab domain (Harappa)
polities.note: Regional domain of the Indus network.

polities.name: Sorath domain (Dholavira, Lothal)
polities.note: Gujarat domain; maritime contact with the Gulf.

polities.name: Painted Grey Ware
polities.note: Material horizon commonly correlated with the later Vedic period.

polities.name: South Indian Megalithic (Iron Age)
polities.note: Iron, urn burials; precedes the Sangam polities.

polities.name: Kuru
polities.note: First well-attested Vedic polity; ritual codification.

polities.name: Panchala
polities.note: Later a mahajanapada; briefly a gana-sangha.

polities.name: Magadha
polities.note: Iron, river control and Rajgir/Pataliputra; eventual victor.

polities.name: Kosala
polities.note: Annexed by Magadha under the Haryankas.

polities.name: Malla
polities.note: Oligarchic; site of the Buddha’s parinirvana.

polities.name: Kuru (late)
polities.note: Reduced to an oligarchy by this period.

polities.name: Achaemenid satrapies (Gandara, Hindush)
polities.note: First imperial administration in the subcontinent.

polities.name: Maurya Empire
polities.note: First subcontinental empire. Ashokan edicts give the first directly attested administrative geography.

polities.name: Satavahana
polities.note: Deccan; start date contested between 3rd and 1st c. BCE.

polities.name: Indo-Greek kingdoms
polities.note: Menander; bilingual coinage is the main evidence.

polities.name: Western Satraps
polities.note: Dated coinage — unusually precise for the period.

polities.name: Kalinga
polities.note: Independent until Ashoka. The one Mauryan conquest with a first-person account of its cost.

polities.name: Mahameghavahana (Kalinga)
polities.note: Kharavela and the Hathigumpha inscription; Kalinga independent again.

polities.name: Gupta Empire
polities.note: Land grants, temple architecture, mathematics and astronomy.

polities.name: Vakataka
polities.note: Ajanta patronage; matrimonially tied to the Guptas.

polities.name: Pushyabhuti (Harsha)
polities.note: Harshavardhana; last great north Indian power before fragmentation.

polities.name: Chalukya of Badami
polities.note: Pulakeshin II halts Harsha at the Narmada.

polities.name: Gurjara-Pratihara
polities.note: One leg of the tripartite struggle for Kannauj.

polities.name: Rashtrakuta
polities.note: Ellora Kailasa; third leg of the tripartite struggle.

polities.name: Chola Empire
polities.note: Maritime reach to Srivijaya; exceptional inscriptional record of village assemblies.

polities.name: Kakatiya
polities.note: Tank irrigation across the Telangana uplands.

polities.name: Ahom kingdom
polities.note: Six centuries; repels the Mughals at Saraighat, 1671.

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate — Mamluk
polities.note: Iltutmish, Razia, Balban. Iqta assignment established.

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate — Khalji
polities.note: Alauddin: price control, market regulation, Deccan raids.

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate — Tughlaq
polities.note: Daulatabad transfer; token currency; Timur’s sack in 1398.

polities.name: Bengal Sultanate
polities.note: Independent, wealthy, and a distinct Bengali literary patron.

polities.name: Bahmani Sultanate
polities.note: First Deccan sultanate; splits into five.

polities.name: Mewar (Sisodia)
polities.note: Rana Sanga, Pratap; the longest Rajput resistance.

polities.name: Mughal Empire
polities.note: Mansabdari and zabt. The Ain-i-Akbari (1595) is the richest pre-colonial dataset in existence for the region.

polities.name: Sur Empire
polities.note: Sher Shah: the rupiya, the Grand Trunk Road, revenue survey.

polities.name: Maratha Confederacy
polities.note: Chauth and sardeshmukhi — a tribute-overlordship system, not territorial annexation.

polities.name: Sikh Misls
polities.note: Twelve confederacies; a genuinely non-monarchic sovereignty model.

polities.name: Sikh Empire
polities.note: Ranjit Singh; last major independent power to fall.

polities.name: Awadh
polities.note: Annexed under the doctrine of lapse’s cousin, misgovernment.

polities.name: Mysore (Wodeyar)
polities.note: Interrupted 1761–1799; later a model developmental state.

polities.name: Mysore under Hyder Ali & Tipu Sultan
polities.note: Rocket artillery, state trading monopolies, four Anglo-Mysore wars.

polities.name: Travancore
polities.note: Early state investment in schooling and public health.

polities.name: Manipur (Ningthouja)
polities.note: Traditional chronology begins 33 CE; reliable from c. 1400.

polities.name: Estado da Índia (Portuguese)
polities.note: Goa, Daman, Diu; annexed by India in 1961.

polities.name: English East India Company
polities.note: Territorial from the 1765 Diwani of Bengal.

polities.name: British Raj
polities.note: Crown rule. Directly administered provinces plus ~565 princely states under paramountcy.

polities.name: Bombay Presidency
polities.note: Ryotwari; cotton and the mill economy.

polities.name: Dominion of India
polities.note: Transition; integration of the princely states.

polities.name: Pakistan
polities.note: Included for boundary and trade context.

polities.name: Bangladesh
polities.note: Included for boundary and trade context.

relations.note: Territorial cession westward after the treaty.
The Kalinga war; Ashoka’s thirteenth rock edict.
Pulakeshin II halts Harsha; no submission either way.
Devagiri pays tribute, then is annexed.
Chauth and sardeshmukhi extracted across Mughal territory.
Treaty of Bassein begins the subsidiary system in the Deccan.
Third Anglo-Maratha war; the Peshwa is pensioned.
